title: How monsters find you
summary: Monsters in R.E.P.O. do not wander blindly: the game tracks the room a player is in and the distance to them, which is how a monster can commit to a chase.
body: The game keeps track of which room a player is in, so a monster can react to where you are rather than only to what it can see.
Distance to a player is tracked as well, which is why closing the gap is something the game can measure rather than approximate.
Because monsters are physical objects, knowing where you are still ends in contact: the tracking gets them there, physics decides what happens next.
What this entry does not tell you: how far a monster can notice you, how fast it moves or how long it commits to a chase. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: The game tracks which room a player is in.
The distance between a monster and a player is tracked.
Monsters are physical objects, so contact is a collision.
The build names a detection sphere of its own, along with the noise a crouch makes.
facts.evidence: asset names: Detection Sphere, Crouch Noise
